holder-quote: Selys slept.
Selys slept.

She turned, blew out the candle on her bed, and lay down. She was so tired. Selys hadn’t ever been more exhausted in her life, not even after fighting for her life against the undead! She had worn herself down. But she felt good. Relaxed. Almost at once, Selys drifted off to sleep.

Selys watched as the two left through the crowd. The Drakes and Gnolls protested as Lism and Krshia’s shouting match continued in the background, but the two members of the City Watch were on business now. So it was Selys’ turn.
She’d turned into a Level 8 [Heiress] as well, but she hadn’t gained a Skill.
Are you a [Heiress], by any chance? That’s the only class I can think of that fits.
Selys grinned. Now this was a job she could handle. Not as an [Heiress]—okay, partly as an [Heiress], but also as her main class. A [Receptionist].
Selys grinned. Now this was a job she could handle. Not as an [Heiress]—okay, partly as an [Heiress], but also as her main class. A [Receptionist].
That was the thing about being a [Heiress]. And being rich, for that matter. Suddenly, everyone had time for you.
Both her eyes and Krshia’s darted sideways to Selys. The Drake [Heiress] held up her claws.
Selys had a big smile on her face as her tail swished back and forth excitedly.
Selys bit her tongue at Zevara’s dismissive tone. But she was also embarrassed. The [Receptionist] turned [Heiress] squared her shoulders a touch indignantly.

Without another word, she hurried back into her inn and found a Drake in the crowd. Selys had heard the commotion, of course, and when Erin explained what had happened, the newly-made [Heiress] gladly accompanied her over to Xif. Erin smiled sweetly at the [Alchemist], who coughed politely.
Hi, I’m Selys. I think we met. I’m a [Receptionist]—er, I mean [Heiress].
“But you did win, Selys. Be happy about that.”
She was Selys Shivertail, [Heiress].
The [Heiress] grinned as the [Merchant] turned to Pisces, giving him a full-toothed smile in the fashion of the Drakes.
Selys was rich. She was an [Heiress], and right now…peeved.

The Gnoll [Builder] grinned. Some of the other Gnolls and Drakes chuckled. The Humans looked relieved. But that only opened the floodgates to more questions. Selys smiled as they began pelting the other Gnolls and Drakes in line with queries.
Selys complained. Erin gave her a betrayed look. The [Heiress] rolled her eyes.
Erin told Selys about the garden, her plans for the day—but the Drake [Heiress] was far more exciting.
In awe, Mrsha stared up at Selys. The [Heiress] beamed.
The [Heiress] was a nice person. So nice, and brave, and kind.

Nor had she asked. She’d assumed—rightly—that she could cover it, whatever it was. Selys Shivertail adjusted her hat and noticed the envious stares. The [Heiress] paused, and again, felt that sense of surreality at her position, the amount of gold she knew she had. But only for a moment. She was getting used to it.
The [Heiress] saw Drassi roll her eyes. Erin laughed as she led Selys down the passage to the door. She waited as a group of Humans came through.
Erin blinked. The Drake, Zekia, looked at Selys. And the [Heiress] saw her step back, confer with one of her squad mates. Then Zekia spoke again.
Even Erin was taken aback. Zekia nodded to Selys and the [Heiress] realized that there was someone waiting for her.
The [Heiress] looked at Sir Relz. And she looked down at her clothes and adjusted her hat as he led her down the street. And she realized—

The Dullahan woman was very formal. But she offered Selys a cordial smile. The [Heiress] looked at her rather riveting armor studded with costly metal and clearly designed for ornamentation rather than combat. Miss Duskal preened like a Garuda under the gaze.
The Drake transferred the drink to her other claw to hold out a claw to shake. Selys stared at her. The [Heiress] folded her arms.
The [Heiress] stared. She saw Onieva wink at her.
Drassi looked at Selys. The [Heiress] was nodding.
The [Heiress] looked at Erin. And this time, it was a long look.
The young woman saw Selys roll her eyes. But the [Heiress] was smiling.
The [Heiress] looked sideways at Erin. She hummed.
Back together with Selys! She was always nice. And now she was an [Heiress], they were really connecting.

Couriers. Selys Shivertail gazed into Rufelt’s mirror. She shivered, as for a second, the image focused on Hawk and the other Couriers. She stared at Hawk. The silly, affable Rabbitman who wooed Drakes in Liscor with carrot-related foods. Who had smashed through a carriage of [Assassins] with his bare fists and feet.
The problem was that it didn’t feel meaningful. Selys, as a [Heiress], had money. She wanted to do something with said money. She confessed her problems to her friends and found…little sympathy.
The [Heiress] felt awkward admitting that. She had more money than she could have ever dreamed of saving and it was change compared to that auction. Hence her state of having too much and too little.
The [Princess] blinked at the Drake [Heiress].
Hawk appeared next to Selys so fast she didn’t see him. As always, the Courier moved like lightning. The [Heiress] turned her head—and scowled.
Zevara played awkwardly with a quill as Selys sat in her office a little bit later. The [Heiress] sniffed. After a second, Zevara offered her handkerchief.
Onieva blinked as she recognized the [Heiress]. She pulled back Mirn, who was poised to chase Selys off.
She gave Selys a smile that instantly managed to be needling. The [Heiress] glowered.
The [Heiress] laughed.
Heck, Selys had realized how much money she needed. She had more money as an [Heiress] than she could ever imagine. And she needed more.
“When we left Liscor, Selys asked me if I would go on a quest for her. To find a missing piece of the Heartflame Set.”

They were going to die. Selys Shivertail sank out of her chair, unable to sit upright. She kept watching, though. Only Mrsha even noticed the Drake fall to the floor. She tugged at Selys, but the [Heiress] couldn’t speak or stand.
Drassi had her arms under Selys’ shoulders and was holding her friend back. Selys whirled around.
Selys, the [Heiress], gave Olesm a flat look
Selys, I have potions
To Selys, it felt like it had flashed by in some senses.
Selys shot back instantly, but Pisces just sniffed
Don’t worry, Selys.
Selys Shivertail ran into the guild followed by a second group.
Selys and Lyonette held out their hands, but Erin beckoned.
you’ve never been to a beach, Selys?
Lyonette was half-screaming as she leaned on Selys’ shoulder, and the [Heiress] was patting her hand.
Selys. The Drake was striding towards her, scales flushed crimson.
Selys got experience in her
As an [Heiress], none of her old friends could relate to her. Selys had gold, but no job.
Haldagaz leapt away as Selys yelped
Selys Shivertail sat in one corner of the coach
Miss Selys Shivertail, we meet again. What is a young [Heiress] doing touring the north?
Selys Shivertail, as you well know. [Heiress].
He beamed as every face turned to Selys.
The Drake [Heiress] croaked a reply.
Selys leaned on a counter and saw Tekshia Shivertail sitting there
Selys glanced around, but there was no one there.
Selys Shivertail just looked up, spotted the real Lyonette, and glared.
Selys Shivertail had not ceased glaring at Lyonette the entire time.
Pleadingly. Selys’ yellow gaze met Lyonette’s—and there was something more than just anger there.
Selys’ yellow gaze met Lyonette’s—and there was something more than just anger there.
She did this while staring Selys down across the room from her.
Now, the [Heiress] was gasping, and her claws were shaking. Lyonette kept going.
You think you have a say? Come at me with a spear in hand as a [Guildmistress].
